*[Image directories]: The build output of an image, images.<variant>-<platform> of chalkos.lib.mkImages: the raw image, systemd-repart's report of its partitions, the definitions of the system region, metadata.json, which names the image's variant, platform, root hash, provenance and kinds, the kinds' JSON Schemas in schemas/ and, on an image with Kubernetes, what it fixes about Kubernetes in image.json.
*[Node certificates]: The certificate chalkd serves and authenticates with, issued by the node CA for the node's name, host name and addresses and valid for one year.

*[node certificates]: The certificate chalkd serves and authenticates with, issued by the node CA for the node's name, host name and addresses and valid for one year.
*[Cluster endpoint]: The URL of the cluster's API server, spec.endpoint of the Cluster document, at which kubelets, kubeconfigs and joining control planes reach it.
*[Config documents]: One object of a node's config, written in YAML in the style of a Kubernetes object: an apiVersion of a group and a version, a kind, a metadata.name and a spec.
*[Fallback keyslot]: The second keyslot of every encrypted partition, which unlocks it when the TPM does not: the node's recovery key by default, a password, or none, as spec.encryption.fallback of the node's SystemDisk chooses.
*[Kubernetes share]: The Kubernetes secrets a node receives at install: on a control plane, the cluster, front-proxy and etcd CAs with their keys, the service-account key, the encryption key and the node CA; on a worker, the cluster CA certificate and a kubelet client certificate.
*[Maintenance mode]: The mode chalkd runs in on a node that is not installed: it serves a self-signed certificate, prints its fingerprint and the node's addresses on the console, and accepts only reads, reboots and an install.

*[Platforms]: The kind of machine an image is built for, such as metal or kvm, named in the platforms argument of chalkos.lib.mkImages with NixOS modules of its own.
*[Root hash]: The top hash of the store's dm-verity hash tree.
*[Rotations]: The replacement of a CA or key with chalkctl rotate, in phases that first trust the new value everywhere, then use it, then re-issue, and last remove the old value.
*[bootstrap]: The one-time start of a cluster's etcd on its first control plane, with chalkctl bootstrap.
*[dm-verity]: The kernel's block-level integrity check: each block of the store is hashed into a hash tree whose top is the root hash, and a block that does not match fails to read.

*[Admin]: The client role that may call every method of the node API but the one nodes renew their certificates with, which needs the role node: install, config changes, volume resets, bootstrap, etcd membership changes and rotations among them.
*[Facts]: Node state a change rule reads, declared in chalkos.facts: the JSON of a file, such as the Kubernetes share, or of a program of the image's store, which chalkd runs in a sandbox.
*[Grant]: The config kinds a unit reads at runtime, as systemd.services.<unit>.chalkos.kinds declares them: chalkd writes their documents below /run/chalkos/config and the values their secretRef fields name into the unit's credentials.
*[OS CA]: The root certificate authority of a cluster's node API: chalkd and chalkctl trust only certificates that chain to it.
*[PCR 7]: The TPM register that measures the Secure Boot state: whether it is on, the PK, KEK, db and dbx contents, and the db certificate that verified the boot binaries.
*[STATE]: A small partition, 128 MiB by default, encrypted and sealed to the TPM by default.
*[Slots]: A pair of partitions that holds one image's store: the erofs data and its dm-verity hash tree, labelled store_<hash16> and store-verity_<hash16> from the first 16 hex characters of its root hash, or _empty.
*[Store]: The read-only Nix store of an image: an erofs file system compressed with zstd, checked by dm-verity on every read.

*[store]: The read-only Nix store of an image: an erofs file system compressed with zstd, checked by dm-verity on every read.
*[Fact]: Node state a change rule reads, declared in chalkos.facts: the JSON of a file, such as the Kubernetes share, or of a program of the image's store, which chalkd runs in a sandbox.
*[Slot]: A pair of partitions that holds one image's store: the erofs data and its dm-verity hash tree, labelled store_<hash16> and store-verity_<hash16> from the first 16 hex characters of its root hash, or _empty.
*[UKIs]: A unified kernel image: the kernel, initrd, kernel command line and os-release in one EFI binary, which systemd-boot loads and Secure Boot verifies.
*[VIPs]: A virtual IP address of the API server, one per IP family, that one healthy control plane holds.
*[fact]: Node state a change rule reads, declared in chalkos.facts: the JSON of a file, such as the Kubernetes share, or of a program of the image's store, which chalkd runs in a sandbox.
*[slot]: A pair of partitions that holds one image's store: the erofs data and its dm-verity hash tree, labelled store_<hash16> and store-verity_<hash16> from the first 16 hex characters of its root hash, or _empty.
*[A/B]: The update scheme of a node's disk: two slots, A and B, each able to hold an image.
*[ESP]: The EFI system partition, a FAT file system at the start of the system disk.
*[Lab]: A cluster that chalklab runs as virtual machines, from a lab file, chalklab.yaml, that names the cluster's inventory and each VM's MAC address, memory, CPUs and disks.
*[TPM]: The machine's Trusted Platform Module 2.0, which seals the keys of STATE, VAR and encrypted volumes to PCR 7, so they unlock without a password only under the same Secure Boot state.
*[UKI]: A unified kernel image: the kernel, initrd, kernel command line and os-release in one EFI binary, which systemd-boot loads and Secure Boot verifies.
*[VAR]: The partition mounted at /var that holds what a node writes: etcd, containerd, the kubelet, logs.
*[VIP]: A virtual IP address of the API server, one per IP family, that one healthy control plane holds.
*[lab]: A cluster that chalklab runs as virtual machines, from a lab file, chalklab.yaml, that names the cluster's inventory and each VM's MAC address, memory, CPUs and disks.
